name: gitcliff-sortorder-v2
instr:
**Release notes went wrong once we reached 1.10.0**

We write CHANGELOG.md and our GitHub release text with git-cliff (latest from main) and the
default config from `git cliff --init`, unchanged. The release job runs
`git cliff --bump --unreleased --prepend CHANGELOG.md`, publishes the bumped version, then fills
the release page with `git cliff --latest`.

Since 1.10.0:

- The v1.10.0 release page got the 1.9.0 notes.
- For 1.10.1, the prepended part had the new section followed by the whole 1.10.0 section
  again, so CHANGELOG.md now lists 1.10.0 twice.

Also, since we updated git-cliff, "💼 Other" shows up right after "🐛 Bug Fixes" inside a
release instead of at the end, where it always was.

The checkout is in /workdir. Could you track down where this actually goes wrong and fix it
there? Please include a regression test, in the tests/ directory of the crate it exercises (say
git-cliff/tests/repro.rs), that fails on the current code because of this problem (a real test
failure, not an import error) and passes once it's fixed.
Test the reported behaviour, not your patch: it should still pass if the bug gets fixed some other correct
way, so no asserting on source text or on helpers only your fix has. It should run on its own
from a clean checkout with just your test files added.

I doubt I'm the only one hitting this. Anything else that goes through that code is probably
wrong too, so please fix it at the source rather than special-casing my input. The fix belongs in
the libr
